title: Sensitive Output Curation and Liability Framing — Operational Annex (Draft)
body:
Purpose and context:

This document is a working draft of an "Operational Annex" intended to sit alongside customer DPAs and Service Agreements. It scopes how Redwood will operationalize: (a) curation and automated redaction of sensitive inference outputs, (b) liveness/availability guarantees for redaction tooling, and (c) a narrowly tailored liability framing that reflects practical mitigations and residual risk.

Audience and status:
- Audience: Legal, Security, Product (Hosted API & Dedicated), Customer Success, and selected enterprise prospects.
- Status: Draft for internal review. Not yet approved for customer use.

High-level approach (one-paragraph summary):
Redwood will offer an "Output Curation & Redaction Annex" as an optional addendum for customers with sensitive workloads. The annex defines categories of sensitive content, operational controls (automated and manual review flows), performance SLAs for redaction decisions, evidence/access for audits, and a limited liability framework that ties customer remedies to Redwood's verified mitigations (redaction performed, logs retained, escalation followed).

Key definitions (operational, not legal-hedged):
- Sensitive Output: any model-generated text identified by the configured policy as falling into one or more categories in the policy (PII, PCI, PHI, Regulated Identifiers, Credentials, or custom customer labels).
- Redaction Action: an automated or manual transformation applied to a returned inference output to remove or mask identified sensitive tokens before delivery to the calling application.
- Redaction Decision Window: the latency budget within which Redwood's redaction pipeline must return a final redacted response (or fallback) to meet the SLA.
- Evidence Bundle: timebound artifacts retained to demonstrate that redaction processes executed as configured (logs, hashes, sample outputs, redaction rationale).

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to Redwood-hosted API and Dedicated (reserved capacity) deployments.
- For Private on-prem/VPC deployments, Redwood will provide a technical spec and templates but cannot commit to evidence exports outside a separate statement of work.
- Annex is opt-in per-customer and per-model. Customers can select from Redwood's pre-built policies or upload a custom policy.

Operational controls (Overview):
1) Policy configuration: customers choose taxonomy (prebuilt: PII/PHI/credentials/regulatory keywords) and sensitivity thresholds. Policies are versioned.
2) Pre-response blocking: if high confidence match and policy configured as "block", the request is halted and a sanitized error returned.
3) Inline redaction: for medium-confidence matches, tokens are masked/obfuscated and returned with metadata flagging redaction.
4) Post-hoc review: customers may enroll an escalation queue that routes outputs to a human-review pool for borderline cases.
5) Feedback loop: customer-provided labels train/adjust heuristic thresholds; changes trigger policy-version rollouts and a brief evaluation window.

Performance and SLA commitments (draft numbers for internal review):
- Redaction decision window: 95th percentile <= 350ms extra on top of model generation latency for inline redaction on Hosted API.
- Blocking fallback latency: error returned within 200ms of generation completion.
- Evidence retention: redaction logs and hash pointers retained for 90 days by default (extendable).
- Outage/fallback: if redaction subsystem is degraded, Redwood will (in order of configured customer preference): (a) temporarily disable redaction and return unredacted responses (with a risk flag), (b) fallback to a lower-latency conservative policy (more aggressive masking), or (c) return errors. Specific fallback order is configurable per-customer and documented in the Console.

Liability framing (principles and proposed carve-outs):
- Principle: Redwood's operational liability should be materially tied to whether the company performed the agreed-upon technical steps (policy run, logging, evidence retention, escalation) rather than absolute prevention of every sensitive token.
- Proposed remedies: for verified failures where Redwood did not execute the configured controls, remedies will be limited to (i) documented remediation steps, (ii) a service credit schedule tied to the severity of control failure, and (iii) assistance with customer notifications where legally required.
- Explicitly excluded losses: consequential damages arising from customer application usage of outputs (business interruption, lost profits) remain excluded except to the extent required by law.
- Time-bounded discovery requirement: customers must notify Redwood within 60 days of becoming aware of an alleged failure for claims tied to operational evidence preserved by Redwood.

Auditability and evidence model:
- Evidence bundle contents: policy version id, input hash, raw generated output (stored encrypted), redaction markers (what was removed/masked), redaction engine logs and decision confidence scores, and the ID of any human reviewer who intervened (if applicable).
- Access model: customers can request evidence exports for their own traffic via the Console or a secure upload link. Exports for legal audits will follow Redwood's standard subpoena/evidence process.
- Privacy note: raw generated outputs are treated as sensitive by default and will be encrypted; access to evidence bundles is scoped to customer admins and to Redwood personnel on a least-privilege basis for support.

Operational runbooks (implementation checklist for engineering & SRE):
- Instrumentation: ensure redaction pipeline emits structured logs and trace IDs. (Linked JIRA: SEC-4523).
- Canary rollout: deploy redaction policy changes behind feature gates and run 7-day canary.
- Monitoring: synthetic probes for redaction latency and false-positive rates; dashboard tile in Console: "Redaction health".
- Incident playbook: predefined severity definitions (S1: systemic redaction failure; S2: policy misconfiguration causing false positives; S3: evidence export failure).

Customer obligations (operationally realistic expectations):
- Policy tuning: customers agree to participate in a 2-week tuning window after enabling a custom policy and to provide labeled examples where feasible.
- Prompt engineering: customers should avoid embedding secrets in prompts and are expected to follow Redwood's prompt safety guidelines (link: confluence:SEC-ops/prompt-safety).
- Notification cooperation: in the event evidence shows an operational failure, customers must cooperate with Redwood in timelines for remediations and notifications.

Data residency and export controls:
- For customers requiring EU-only retention, evidence bundles will be stored in the EU region if the customer's account is configured to enforce EU data residency.
- Exports: full evidence export may include raw outputs; Redwood will support redaction of customer-specified fields prior to external export.

Open legal/technical questions (for Legal + Product workshop):
- Degree of liability cap tied specifically to redaction subsystem vs. overall platform.
- Whether customers can require periodic third-party attestations of redaction accuracy (scope/cost).
- How to codify acceptable fallback order (disable redaction vs. aggressive masking) in the Annex.

Next steps and proposed timeline:
- Internal review weeks 1–2 (Legal + Security + Product) — collect feedback and resolve liability principle.
- Prototype evidence export UI (Engineering) — 3 sprints.
- Pilot with 2 enterprise customers under NDA — month 2–3.
- Finalize Annex language for inclusion in the DPA addendum library — month 4.

References and links:
- confluence:SEC-ops/sensitive-output-guidelines (policy taxonomy)
- JIRA SEC-4523 (implementation work)
- github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/412 (redaction engine prototype)
- slack:#sec-prod (ongoing thread)

Notes to reviewers (things we want explicit guidance on):
1) Legal: recommended phrasing for the time-bounded discovery requirement and whether 60 days is defensible.
2) Product: are the proposed latency budgets operationally achievable for Dedicated customers with pinned models?
3) Sales/CS: how to position the annex (value vs. non-monetary risk transfer) in enterprise negotiations.

Change log (tracking major edits):
- 2025-02-10: initial draft (A. Chen)
- 2025-02-18: added SLA numbers & evidence retention defaults (M. Ortiz)
- 2025-02-27: inserted fallback options and customer obligations section (L. Nguyen)

End of draft.

(Attached: informal test outputs and a short sample evidence bundle exported from the trial redaction pipeline are linked in the JIRA ticket).
